findings.title: the finished-run waste surfaces only fire on `complete`, never on `accepting` — the state a fully-merged run actually reaches without an operator verb (`orchid_run_status_terminal`, lib/common.sh:1362), so `orchid doctor` prints `ok:` for exactly the schedule the finding is about

a spent wake budget on the one recorded boundary declines the orchestrator wake for the whole run, so a second, genuinely settleable boundary that appears later is never woken for and is also skipped by the notify loop (`drive_boundary_wakes_orchestrator` → `continue`), leaving it silently starved

the pump's deleted-target refusal is unobservable under the schedulers orchid itself installs — the rendered plist sets `StandardErrorPath`/`StandardOutPath` to `/dev/null` and the cron line redirects both, and a nonzero exit from a `StartInterval` agent has no operator-visible failure accounting, contradicting the "the scheduler's own failure accounting sees it" claim in runners/orchid-pump:96 and PROTOCOL.md
